First-time setup

Getting Started

Complete these in order. The planner updates this checklist automatically as you save and verify your setup.

0 of 4 complete
Start by creating your profile.
Important: this planner is a personal recordkeeping and calculation tool. Reference records do not replace a prescription or prove product identity, strength, sterility or suitability. Confirm the actual product, dose, concentration, route, schedule, storage requirement and use/discard instructions with a qualified prescriber or dispensing pharmacist.

First-time setup

1

Complete your profile in Account

Start with Account → Profile. Enter the information used for progress tracking, including name, DOB, height, starting weight, target weight and tracking start date. Optional health context and notes can be added when useful.

The planner uses one profile. You do not need to enter a second profile in Progress.
2

Add your treatment in Treatments

Open Treatments and work through the form from top to bottom:

  • Choose a Knowledge Base reference record or enter the treatment manually.
  • Enter the prescribed dose, route, schedule, start date and time.
  • Enter the actual vial strength, BAC water/final prepared volume and syringe/device.
  • Review the calculated syringe marking.
  • Configure an active/break cycle only when one applies.
  • Configure schedule, interval and weekdays directly in each cycle when needed.
3

Review and verify before activation

After a treatment is added, review the summary and verify the actual product, route, dose, strength, final volume, schedule, syringe/device and storage/use-discard instructions against your prescription, dispensing label or clinician/pharmacist instructions.

Only a verified treatment should populate Today.
4

Use Today for daily actions

Once setup is complete, Today becomes your normal home screen. Review treatments due, mark completed administrations Done, and check vial reminders.

5

Record outcomes in Progress

Use Progress for new weight or waist measurements, notes, trend charts, progress history and administration history. Your profile itself remains managed in Account.

6

Use Reference when you need supporting information

Reference contains the Knowledge Base, Administration & Safety guide and this Full User Guide. It supports setup and daily use but is not a required daily workflow.

7

Use Account for sync, backup and account tools

Your approved account syncs supported planner records across signed-in sessions and devices. JSON export remains an additional portable backup for recovery or offline safekeeping.

Backups may contain sensitive health information. Store them securely.

Everyday use

1 · Open Today Check what is due and any vial reminders.
2 · Record completion Mark the administration Done so history stays current.
3 · Update Progress Add measurements or notes when you want to track outcomes.

Complete navigation guide

Navigate and Maximize the Planner

Use this as the full operating guide after initial setup. Screenshots show the actual planner layout; controls may display different values depending on your account and treatments.

1. Getting Started

New and incomplete accounts land here first. Follow the four setup steps in sequence. A completed profile unlocks treatment setup; adding a treatment leads to verification; verification leads to Today.

  • Use the highlighted step to continue where you left off.
  • The checklist updates automatically from saved planner data.
  • Returning users with completed setup continue to land on Today.

2. Account & Profile

Maintain one personal profile under Account. This profile supplies Progress and goal-tracking context.

  • Complete name, DOB, height, starting weight and target weight for onboarding.
  • Keep optional health context and notes concise and current.
  • Use Account for cloud status, backup/transfer, email-change requests and account tools.

3. Treatments

Treatments is the source of truth for the schedule used by Today. Build each treatment from the prescribed schedule and the actual vial/preparation in hand.

  • Use the Treatments field guide search when a label or calculation is unfamiliar.
  • Enter route, vial strength, water/final volume, syringe/device and disposal period accurately.
  • Configure cycles and dose phases only when they apply to the prescribed plan.
  • Vial Schedule uses the actual scheduled dose for each administration date when calculating Full Dose and Cycle Dose.

4. Review & Verify

Verification is the safety gate before a treatment drives Today. Review the treatment card against the prescription, dispensing label or clinician/pharmacist instructions.

  • Check product, route, dose, strength, final prepared volume, schedule and device.
  • Confirm storage and use/discard instructions.
  • Do not verify until the displayed plan matches the actual instructions and product.
  • If the regimen changes, update the treatment and verify the revised setup again.
Why this mattersToday is intentionally gated by verification. This reduces the chance of a draft or incomplete treatment appearing as a daily action.

5. Today

Today is the daily action screen after setup. Use it to see what is due, record completed administrations and watch vial-related reminders.

  • Mark an administration Done only after it actually occurs.
  • Completion updates administration history automatically.
  • Use vial reminders and purchase prompts as planning aids, then reconcile them with your real inventory.
  • If Today is unexpectedly empty, check treatment status, start date, schedule and verification.

6. Progress

Progress is for outcomes and history, not a second profile. Record measurements and use charts/history to review changes over time.

  • Add measurements consistently using the same measurement method.
  • Use notes for context that may explain a change in the trend.
  • Review administration history when reconciling missed or completed doses.
  • Your personal profile remains managed under Account.

7. Reference

Reference contains supporting information: the searchable Knowledge Base, Administration & Safety material, and this guide.

  • Search Knowledge Base records by peptide/treatment name or relevant keyword.
  • Use source information as reference only; it does not replace an individualized prescription.
  • Use Administration & Safety for route/device concepts and supporting explanations.

8. Mobile use

The same workflow is available on mobile. Content stacks vertically and the main navigation stays accessible at the bottom of the screen.

  • Use Getting Started to continue incomplete setup.
  • Use the bottom navigation to move between Today, Treatments, Progress, Reference and Account.
  • Forms and Vial Schedule adapt to the narrower layout without changing the underlying calculations.
  • For long treatment forms, work from top to bottom and save before switching sections.

Best practices to maximize the planner

Keep Treatments currentUpdate changes to dose, schedule, product preparation or cycle before relying on Today.
Record Done promptlyCompletion history is most useful when it reflects what actually happened.
Use actual vial dataVial strength, final volume and discard rules affect units and vial planning.
Review before verificationVerification should represent a deliberate check, not simply a way to unlock Today.
Back up before major editsCloud sync supports normal use; JSON export gives you an additional portable recovery copy.
Use one profileAccount owns your profile; Progress is for measurements, charts and history.

Common checks when something does not look right

IssueCheck first
Nothing appears in TodayConfirm the treatment is active/soon as appropriate, has started, has a valid scheduled dose, and is reviewed/verified.
Units look wrongRecheck vial strength, final prepared volume, dose-entry mode, syringe/device and the scheduled dose for that phase/date.
Vial counts look unexpectedCheck the actual scheduled dose sequence, vial capacity, open/finish dates and discard date. Full Dose ignores discard date; Cycle Dose stops on/before discard.
Progress data is missingConfirm you are signed into the intended account and cloud sync has completed; then check the portable backup if needed.
A treatment changedEdit Treatments first, review the updated summary, then re-verify before relying on Today.

Reference · Knowledge Base

Peptides, compounds, blends and treatment reference records

Search the reference records below. Treatments uses these records for built-in names, variants, strengths, preparation choices, source protocol phases and cycle options. Adding an item does not activate its schedule automatically.

How to read this Knowledge Base
Half-lifeHow long it takes the amount of a substance in the body to fall by about half. It does not by itself define a safe redosing interval.
SubQ / SCSubcutaneous administration into tissue beneath the skin.
IMIntramuscular administration into muscle tissue.
mcg / mgMicrograms and milligrams. 1,000 mcg = 1 mg.
IUInternational Units: a measure of biological activity. It is not a universal weight conversion.
ReconstitutionPreparing a lyophilized product with the verified diluent and volume specified for that product.
TitrationA planned dose progression over time rather than beginning at the final dose.
Starting phaseThe initial treatment phase before any maintenance phase.
Maintenance phaseA later phase intended to maintain the protocol after the starting phase.
WashoutA planned period without scheduled treatment between active cycles.
EODEvery other day.
FastedA source-defined timing instruction related to food intake. Follow the specific product or clinician instruction.
Source conflictTwo source records give materially different protocol information. The planner flags the difference instead of silently choosing one.
Evidence / statusThe source-stated evidence or development context. Research, investigational and approved-medication records are kept distinct.
Source hierarchy used for KB review: official label / regulator → peer-reviewed human evidence → registered clinical trial → peer-reviewed preclinical evidence → secondary educational source → community/vendor protocol.
Treatments

Add, verify and manage your treatments

Work in order: choose the treatment, enter the prescribed schedule, enter the actual product preparation, then configure a cycle only when needed. Changes update Today and Progress automatically.

Treatments field guide
Treatment / PeptideThe peptide, compound, blend or treatment record being added to Treatments.
Prescribed dose (mg)The actual prescribed dose in milligrams used to initialise the treatment schedule.
Medication in vial (mg)The total medication amount contained in the vial before preparation, in milligrams.
BAC water added (mL)The actual volume of bacteriostatic water added to prepare the vial.
Final prepared volume (mL)The final liquid volume after preparation. It is used with vial strength to calculate concentration.
Calculated syringe markingThe syringe-unit marking calculated from the scheduled dose, prepared concentration and syringe calibration.
Vial estimate (auto)An automatic estimate of vial use based on the current preparation and the actual scheduled doses.
StatusThe treatment or vial state currently recorded by the planner.
RouteHow the treatment is administered. Use the route on the actual dispensing label or prescriber instructions.
Vial (mg)The total amount of peptide or compound in one vial, in milligrams.
Water (mL)The volume of diluent added to prepare the vial, in millilitres.
Concentration (mg/mL)The prepared strength calculated from vial milligrams and final prepared liquid volume.
Dispose byThe allowed use period after a vial is opened. The planner uses this period to calculate the discard date.
SyringeThe syringe calibration and capacity used for unit calculations.
CycleControls whether the treatment is continuous or uses active and break periods.
Cycles per year / Cycles/yearThe intended number of complete treatment cycles in one year. Continuous treatment removes routine cycle breaks.
Active / OnThe number of active treatment weeks in the treatment cycle.
Break / OffThe planned treatment-free or washout period after an active cycle.
Cycle StartThe start date of the current or relevant treatment cycle.
Cycle EndThe final active date of the current or relevant treatment cycle.
ScheduleHow often the treatment is scheduled, based on the selected interval or weekdays.
Dose (units)The syringe-unit amount calculated for the scheduled dose using the prepared concentration and syringe calibration.
Dose left in vialEstimated complete scheduled doses remaining in the actively used vial after administrations recorded as given.
Vials per cycleThe current vial number compared with the total vials calculated for the cycle.
Cycle countHow many cycles have started in the current annual plan compared with the configured cycles per year.
Current cycleThe treatment phase that applies now, such as Starting Phase, a numbered cycle or Break.
Next cycle eligibleThe earliest calculated date the next cycle can begin under the configured annual cycle limit.
Start dateThe date the cycle or continuous treatment begins.
TimeThe scheduled administration time for the cycle or continuous treatment.
IntervalThe number of days between administrations when the schedule uses Every N days.
Vial #The sequential vial number in the treatment's calculated Vial Schedule.
Full DoseThe number of complete administrations the vial can supply using the actual scheduled dose for each administration date, ignoring the discard date.
Cycle DoseThe number of complete administrations the vial can supply on or before the discard date, using the actual scheduled dose for each administration date and the vial's remaining capacity.
Open / Date OpenThe date the vial is opened for use.
Finish / Date FinishThe date of the last complete scheduled administration assigned to the vial under the current Vial Schedule.
Start weekThe first treatment week that uses a Dose Schedule row.
End weekThe last treatment week that uses a Dose Schedule row.
DaysThe interval in days for the dose phase when specific weekdays are not selected.
Dose (mg)The actual scheduled dose in milligrams for administrations covered by the Dose Schedule row.
UnitsThe syringe-unit equivalent of the scheduled milligram dose at the current prepared concentration.
WeekdaysThe specific days of the week on which the dose phase is scheduled.
Split doseDivides one scheduled total dose into multiple administrations while keeping the row's total scheduled dose unchanged.
Vial Schedule counting rule: Full Dose and Cycle Dose follow the dose assigned to each actual administration date. They do not apply one current dose to every administration in the vial.

Reference · Administration & Safety

Medical-source administration, syringe and safe-use guide

The diagrams below are original simplified redraws based on current patient/clinical guidance from MedlinePlus, CDC, NHS hospitals and BD medical-device references. They are reminders after training—not a substitute for product-specific instructions or hands-on teaching.

Do

  • Use the route, dose, device and schedule actually prescribed for the product.
  • Use a new sterile needle and syringe for each administration and each vial entry.
  • Wash and dry your hands, work on a clean surface, and keep the needle sterile.
  • Inspect the intended site and rotate sites when the medication instructions permit it.
  • Place used sharps directly into an approved puncture-resistant sharps container.

Don't

  • Do not change between subcutaneous, intramuscular or intravenous routes without clinical direction.
  • Do not reuse or share needles, syringes, cartridges or pens.
  • Do not inject through skin that is red, bruised, swollen, scarred, tender or otherwise abnormal.
  • Do not treat the number printed as syringe “units” as the medication dose unless the prescription explicitly uses that device scale.
  • Do not attempt IV self-injection from this guide.

How the syringe is held for common injection routes

These diagrams show hand position and general needle orientation only. Needle length, gauge, exact angle and whether skin is pinched or stretched depend on the medication, device, body tissue and training you received.

Subcutaneous (SC/SQ)

45° or 90°*

MedlinePlus describes holding the syringe like a pencil and inserting into a skin/fat fold; the angle may be 90° or 45° depending on tissue and the technique taught. Some devices/needle lengths use different handling.

Medical sources: MedlinePlus SQ injections and Cambridge University Hospitals patient guidance. MedlinePlus · CUH NHS

Intramuscular (IM)

90°

CDC guidance uses a 90° insertion for IM administration. Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS self-injection guidance for prescribed B12 demonstrates an outer-thigh site with the skin held taut and muscle relaxed.

Medical sources: CDC adult IM administration and Guy’s & St Thomas’ NHS self-injection guidance. CDC · Guy’s & St Thomas’ NHS

Intravenous (IV)

Professional

This tracker does not provide an IV self-injection technique. IV access and administration require appropriate clinical training, equipment, medication-specific checks and monitoring.

Safety source: CDC Injection Safety. CDC Injection Safety
IntranasalNo injection needle. Use the supplied nasal device and product instructions.
OralUse the labelled oral formulation/device. Oral syringes are not injection syringes.
Sublingual / buccalPlaced under the tongue or against the cheek only when the product is specifically formulated for that route.
TopicalApply only as directed to the specified skin area; this is not an injection route.

Injection sites

This medical illustration shows common subcutaneous insulin injection areas. It is a site-reference image only; do not assume that every injectable medicine or peptide uses the same route or sites.

Subcutaneous injection-site rotation reference

User-provided reference image. Follow the route and injection-site instructions for the specific prescribed product and the technique taught by your clinician.

Subcutaneous injection-site reference

Type 1 Support identifies the abdomen, upper outer thighs, upper buttocks and back/outer upper arms as approved subcutaneous insulin injection areas. The source also notes that insulin absorption speed can vary by site. For non-insulin treatment, use only the route and site taught or prescribed for that specific medicine.

Image/source: Support (BETTER project / IRCM / McGill University)
Source: Type 1 Support — Insulin Absorption Rate Fluctuation Depending on Injection Site
Route reminder: the image above is for subcutaneous insulin injection. Intramuscular, intravenous, intranasal, oral, sublingual/buccal and topical routes use different techniques and/or sites. Follow the medication-specific instructions from the prescriber, pharmacist or official product information.

Safety checks before using the planner

Unapproved peptides: regulators warn that unapproved peptides may have unreliable identity, strength, labelling, sterility, and safety. Confirm that each product is lawfully prescribed and supplied by an authorised pharmacy.
Do not rely on social-media units: the same milligram dose can equal different syringe units at different concentrations. Copy the total vial amount and final prepared volume from the actual dispensing instructions.
Selank and Semax: FDA identifies potential immunogenicity concerns and insufficient safety information for compounded Selank acetate and Semax.
GHK-Cu: TGA specifically lists GHK-Cu among unapproved peptide products and warns of contamination, infection, allergic reactions, and unknown short- and long-term risks.
NAD/NAD+: FDA has reported serious reactions and excessive endotoxin in some compounded NAD+ products. Ingredient grade and sterile manufacturing matter.
Urgent symptoms: seek urgent medical care for breathing difficulty, facial/throat swelling, fainting, severe or persistent abdominal/chest pain, uncontrolled shaking, confusion, repeated vomiting, or another rapidly worsening reaction.

Unit conversion used

Concentration: vial amount (mg) ÷ final prepared volume (mL).
Volume: planned dose (mg) ÷ concentration (mg/mL).
Syringe units: volume (mL) × syringe calibration (units/mL).
A mathematically correct answer can still be unsafe if any source value, route, product identity, sterility, prescription, or syringe is wrong.

Official safety references

TGA: warnings on importing, compounding, and using unapproved peptide products; FDA: compounding risks for Selank, Semax, GHK-Cu and NAD+.

TGA warning: importing unapproved peptides · TGA safety considerations · FDA compounding substances with safety risks · FDA NAD+ sterile compounding warning · CDC safe injection practices · FDA sharps safety

Food, hydration and vitamins

Food and hydration

  • Use a balanced eating pattern with adequate protein, vegetables/fruit, whole-food carbohydrate sources and healthy fats unless your clinician has given you a different plan.
  • Maintain hydration appropriate for your health needs, particularly if appetite is reduced or gastrointestinal symptoms occur.
  • Follow medication-specific food or fasting instructions from the official product information, prescriber or pharmacist.

Vitamins and supplements

  • There is no universal vitamin stack that should automatically accompany peptide treatment.
  • Prefer meeting nutrient needs through food; use supplements for a documented deficiency, dietary gap or other clinician-directed reason.
  • Check vitamins, minerals, herbal products and other supplements with a clinician/pharmacist because interactions, duplicate ingredients and excessive doses are possible.

Medical sources used for this tab

Technique/site guidance: Type 1 Support (BETTER project / IRCM / McGill University) insulin injection-site reference; MedlinePlus Subcutaneous Injections; Cambridge University Hospitals heparin self-injection; CDC adult IM vaccine administration; Guy’s & St Thomas’ NHS intramuscular B12 self-injection. Syringe images/capacities: Patient Care Corporation (BD), WA Health and B. Braun; dosing-error safety: FDA. Safe injection: CDC Injection Safety; sharps: FDA.
